question: What type of epithelial tissue is the outer skin made of?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Stratified squamous epithelium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The outer layer of the skin, also known as the **epidermis**, is primarily composed of **stratified squamous epithelium**. This tissue type is specialized to provide protection against mechanical stress, pathogens, and dehydration.
 
• **Stratified squamous epithelium** consists of multiple layers of cells, with the outermost layer being keratinized (hardened) to form a tough, protective barrier.
 
• This tissue type is particularly suited for areas exposed to friction and wear, such as the surface of the skin, due to its ability to regenerate quickly through mitotic activity in the basal layers.
 
• The keratinized layer of the epidermis is made up of dead cells filled with the protein **keratin**, which is essential for waterproofing and enhancing the skin's mechanical strength.
